chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: Opinions on fusion, free jazz and rock
summary: Smith likes good jazz but not music that is too far out, finds rock unchanged, and plays for the audience that pays.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: That answers that. What do you think of Jazz today?
I mean, do you listen to that Fusion stuff and all that?
What about all that Free stuff?

Well, I don't care too much about that. I like Jazz... When they're playing that good Jazz, I like that all right. But when they get playin' stuff too way out... In other words, it's mostly this Rock-and-Roll stuff. There's no improvement in it. It's the same thing. Some of these big bands now playing some of that Rock-and-Roll, they got a little more polish to it. Yeah, that's all right.

But there's a tendency, you see, for this sort of...like this Jazz-Rock stuff, this Fusion music, and it's like it's 16 bars all on one chord, and then they shift it up a tone or a sub-tone, and play another 16 bars or 32 bars.
What do you think of that?
Well, it's all right. That's the education in the music.
I mean, do you like it?
Yeah, it's all right. I like it all right.
Don't you prefer something with slightly more melodic interest?

Yeah, for myself. Playing myself, I'd rather play something a little more supple(?). I'm mostly interested in the person who's out there listening. In other words, the one that's paying to come in there to hear you is the (?). I've found out that's better. I feel better when I'm playing... Like them people were last night. That kind of audience. They ask for them old numbers -- because I don't care about playing all of them old numbers, too far back. But that's what they like up there, and that's easy on us. I can sit up there and go to sleep playing that!
